status: Approved as drafted by the human reviewer; no amendments
verdict_scoring: 1 for an expected verdict, 0.5 for an acceptable_partial verdict that meets its stated condition, 0 otherwise. Design review cases score priority order instead.

scenarios.tests: Pursue when evidence is observed, the change is cheap and reversible, and research would cost about as much as building
decisive_insights: Demand is observed behaviour from paying accounts (tickets, manual workaround, support time), not stated interest
Two days behind a feature flag is cheap and reversible; five interviews would cost similar time and are unlikely to change the decision
Measure export use and the fall in support export requests; guard that exports respect existing access permissions and match on-screen totals
traps: Recommends interviews or other discovery before building
Invents revenue, churn or conversion figures

scenarios.tests: Pursue a bounded build when a comparison pilot already exists; catch consent and cost risks
decisive_insights: A four-week pilot with a comparison group plus clinics already paying for a workaround is credible evidence; the remaining risk is delivery, not demand
Patient consent, opt-out and messaging rules must be handled; message cost and who pays need deciding
Volunteer clinics may not generalise, so roll out in stages and keep measuring no-shows against non-adopting clinics
traps: Asks for more research before building
Ignores consent or opt-out
Treats the 19%-to-11% drop as a guaranteed result

scenarios.tests: Park a large but off-strategy, unsigned deal; weigh opportunity cost

acceptable_partial.condition: Commits no engineering now and makes any further step depend on a signed, paid commitment or an explicit strategy change

decisive_insights: The deal conflicts with the stated strategy of winning one-to-five-site independents
Two of five engineers for two quarters is a large opportunity cost against the core segment, plus ongoing enterprise support
The promise is conditional and unsigned; state what would reopen it (signed paid commitment, or a deliberate strategy change)
traps: Pursues because of contract size
Treats the conditional promise as a commitment

scenarios.tests: Park despite sunk cost when observed behaviour shows no value

acceptable_partial.condition: Stops the two-month personalisation build and limits any further spend to a small, time-boxed learning step

decisive_insights: Observed trial (9%) and repeat use (1.2%) are low, and basket value showed no uplift
Personalisation does not address why 91% never opened it or why users did not return; five months spent is a sunk cost
Record what was learned and set a condition for revisiting
traps: Approves the personalisation work
Recommends open-ended further investigation

scenarios.tests: Reshape a solution-shaped request toward the need the evidence shows
decisive_insights: 62 of 100 sampled emails concern two processes whose form is buried and whose policy is a 40-page PDF; the need is finding and completing those processes
Surface both forms and short step-by-step answers where employees look first; a chatbot is a solution embedded in the request
Measure emails on those two topics; reconsider a chatbot only if a long tail of varied questions remains
traps: Builds or scopes the chatbot
Ignores the sampled email evidence

scenarios.tests: Reshape away from a vanity engagement metric toward the observed value driver
decisive_insights: Retention is associated with connecting a bank account, and 22% of connection attempts fail at three banks: users show intent and hit a fault
Fix those connection failures and give a clear retry or recovery path before adding attention mechanics
Measure week-one connection success and 90-day retention, not DAU/MAU; note the connection-retention link is correlational
traps: Endorses streaks or push notifications as the priority
Uses DAU/MAU as the primary success measure

scenarios.tests: Investigate quickly when pressure comes from a competitor rather than customer evidence

acceptable_partial.condition: Does not commit the six-week copilot build before checking customer or loss evidence

decisive_insights: A competitor launch is not evidence of customer value or of lost deals
The cheapest evidence is already in hand: review the 22 lost-deal notes and ask recent lost prospects; decide within days
Slow report loading is the observed top complaint and should not be dropped for an unvalidated feature
traps: Commits to the six-week copilot
Dismisses the competitor without checking the evidence
Invents market statistics

scenarios.tests: Catch a causal claim drawn from a correlation and a forced step that harms a segment

acceptable_partial.condition: Replaces the mandatory step with an optional prompt tested against a randomised holdout

decisive_insights: The 2.1x figure is likely selection: users who already work in teams both create workspaces and retain
Forcing the step burdens the 30% of solo freelancers and may reduce onboarding completion
Test causally with a randomised holdout; measure retention with onboarding completion as a guardrail
traps: Approves the mandatory onboarding step
Parks the idea without proposing a test

scenarios.tests: Design review: rank blockers correctly and avoid papering over faults with help text
decisive_insights: Blocker: a common sort-code format is rejected and all fields are cleared; accept spaces and hyphens, keep input and show a field-level error

Blocker: no pending state or effective date; show what happens next and which payment uses the new account, and show 'pending' on the dashboard. Uncertainty risks missed or duplicate payments and drives support calls
Polish after blockers: give Submit a primary style distinct from Cancel; verify with an unassisted task and track 'did my change work?' calls
traps: Leads with button styling or visual polish
Adds help text or a tour instead of fixing validation and status
Invents processing times or research findings

scenarios.tests: Pursue a cheap randomised test without designing a dark pattern
decisive_insights: A large stated-reason sample, a three-day build and a built-in random split make building the test cheaper than more research
Measure net retention or reactivation over a fixed window against the control half, not pause clicks
Pause must be offered, not obstruct cancellation: cancelling stays as easy as today; watch complaints and paused customers who never resume
traps: Asks for more research first
Designs the pause as an obstacle to cancelling
Claims retention will rise by about 38%
